gaja_kesari_yoga.name: Gajakesari Yoga
gaja_kesari_yoga.rule: Jupiter in a kendra from Moon.
gaja_kesari_yoga.practitioner_explanation: Jupiter placed in a kendra (1st/4th/7th/10th) from the Moon. Strength starts strong when Jupiter is conjunct the Moon (house 1) and moderate for the other three kendras, then shifts one step down if either participant is debilitated, or one step up if either is exalted or in its own sign.
gaja_kesari_yoga.lay_explanation: Jupiter sits in a supportive angle from your Moon — a classically favorable combination often read as steadiness paired with good judgment.
gaja_kesari_yoga.strength_rubric: strong if Jupiter is in house 1 from Moon (conjunction), else moderate for house 4/7/10; then one step down if Moon or Jupiter is debilitated, one step up if either is exalted or in its own sign (debilitation takes precedence).
caveats: Classical texts also weigh Jupiter's own dignity, aspects, and any affliction beyond this kendra check — treat as a starting signal, not the complete picture.
notes: Strength should consider Jupiter dignity, Moon strength, aspects, and affliction.

chandra_mangal_yoga.name: Chandra-Mangal Yoga
chandra_mangal_yoga.rule: Moon and Mars conjoin or mutually oppose.
chandra_mangal_yoga.practitioner_explanation: Moon and Mars share a sign (conjunction) or sit in mutual opposition (7th from each other). Strength is strong for exact conjunction and moderate for opposition; no further dignity adjustment is applied.
chandra_mangal_yoga.lay_explanation: Moon and Mars are linked in your chart — traditionally associated with drive paired with emotional intensity, expressed well or poorly depending on the rest of the chart.
chandra_mangal_yoga.strength_rubric: strong if Moon and Mars share a sign (conjunction), moderate if in mutual opposition.
caveats: Result language varies by dignity, house, and benefic/malefic influence in classical texts — this flag doesn't grade those separately.
notes: Result language varies by dignity, house, and benefic/malefic influence.

budhaditya_yoga.name: Budhaditya Yoga
budhaditya_yoga.rule: Sun and Mercury in the same sign.

source_refs.detail: Commonly cited Parashari yoga; exact edition reference pending

budhaditya_yoga.practitioner_explanation: Sun and Mercury share a sign. Always graded moderate — no dignity or combustion adjustment is applied, even though Mercury this close to the Sun is frequently near-combust by definition.
budhaditya_yoga.lay_explanation: Sun and Mercury share a sign — often read as sharpened intellect and clearer communication.
budhaditya_yoga.strength_rubric: always moderate when active; no upgrade/downgrade for dignity or combustion is applied in this implementation.
caveats: Mercury's own dignity and combustion status (near-unavoidable this close to the Sun) should temper the reading; neither is folded into strength here yet.
notes: Combustion and Mercury dignity should temper strength.

kemadruma_yoga.name: Kemadruma Yoga
kemadruma_yoga.rule: Moon lacks classical support in adjacent signs and kendras from Moon.

source_refs.detail: Kemadruma and cancellation rules vary by edition

kemadruma_yoga.practitioner_explanation: Active when no classical planet besides the Sun sits adjacent to the Moon (2nd/12th sign) or in a kendra from the Moon. Graded strong whenever active — this is a binary, conservative flag rather than a fully cancellation-aware implementation.
kemadruma_yoga.lay_explanation: Your Moon lacks other planets nearby or in a few key supportive positions — a classical caution flag about needing to build your own support systems, not a fixed outcome.
kemadruma_yoga.strength_rubric: binary: active = strong, inactive = none — no partial grading.
caveats: Numerous classical cancellation rules exist (e.g. Moon in a kendra from Lagna, benefic aspects on the Moon) that are not yet all implemented; treat this as a conservative, simplified flag pending fuller cancellation logic.
source_status: convention_dependent — traditions differ on what counts as 'support'.
notes: Cancellation rules vary; AstroSpace currently uses a conservative simplified flag.

neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga.name: Neecha Bhanga Raja Yoga
neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga.rule: Debilitated planet receives cancellation through debilitation sign lord or related kendra conditions.

source_refs.detail: Neecha Bhanga conditions; complete exception set pending

neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga.practitioner_explanation: For each debilitated classical planet, checks whether the lord of its debilitation sign is placed in a kendra from Lagna or from the Moon; either condition reports a cancellation trigger. Always graded moderate when triggered — the number of conditions met is not graded separately.
neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga.lay_explanation: A weak (debilitated) placement in your chart may be getting classical backup that offsets the weakness, turning a caution into something more workable.
neecha_bhanga_raja_yoga.strength_rubric: always moderate when triggered; no further grading by how many cancellation conditions are simultaneously met.
caveats: Only checks 'debilitation-sign-lord in kendra from Lagna/Moon'; BPHS documents several additional Neecha Bhanga conditions (e.g. exchange with the debilitated planet, exaltation-sign-lord conditions) not yet implemented.
verified: false — pending fuller validation against a complete exception set.
notes: Current implementation checks debilitation sign lord in kendra from Lagna or Moon only.

raja_yoga.name: Raja Yoga
raja_yoga.practitioner_explanation: For every kendra-lord/trikona-lord pair (excluding cases where one planet lords both), reports one instance when they share a sambandha — conjunction, mutual aspect (including mutual 7th), parivartana exchange, or a one-way graha drishti. Strength starts moderate for a mutual connection or weak for a one-way aspect, then shifts one step for participant dignity.
raja_yoga.lay_explanation: Two of your chart's most influential house-lords are connected — a classical marker for authority, achievement, and standing, more so when the connection is a strong mutual link rather than a one-way glance.
raja_yoga.strength_rubric: moderate if mutual sambandha (conjunction / mutual aspect / parivartana), weak if only a one-way graha drishti; then one step down if a participant is debilitated, one step up if a participant is exalted or in its own sign (debilitation takes precedence).
caveats: Full strength assessment (house condition, additional aspects, divisional/varga support) is pending; this is an association-detection pass, not a complete Raja Yoga strength model.
verified: false.
notes: Implementation includes conjunction, opposition, parivartana exchange, and special graha drishti for Mars/Jupiter/Saturn; full strength assessment pending.

caveats: Full strength assessment (house condition, additional aspects, divisional/varga support) is pending; this is an association-detection pass, not a complete Dhana Yoga strength model.

sunapha_yoga.practitioner_explanation: Any of Mars/Mercury/Jupiter/Venus/Saturn occupies the 2nd sign from the Moon; graded moderate. When both the 2nd and 12th from Moon are occupied, Durudhara Yoga (strong) subsumes this, and Sunapha is still reported alongside it with a 'subsumed' note rather than being suppressed.

When Durudhara Yoga is also active, Sunapha is reported alongside it with a 'subsumed' note, not replaced.

source_refs.detail: Chandra yogas; exact edition reference pending

durudhara_yoga.practitioner_explanation: Both the 2nd and 12th signs from the Moon are occupied by at least one of Mars/Mercury/Jupiter/Venus/Saturn. Graded strong — this is the combined, stronger form of Sunapha and Anapha, which remain reported alongside it with a subsumed note.
durudhara_yoga.lay_explanation: Both flanks of your Moon are occupied by planets — the combined, stronger version of Sunapha and Anapha, traditionally read as support arriving from more than one direction.

caveats: Requires both flanking signs occupied simultaneously; a single flank occupied is Sunapha or Anapha alone, not Durudhara.
notes: When active, Sunapha and Anapha are still reported with a subsumed note.
